newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka stocks close at 26-month high.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka stocks close at 26-month high.

text.p: Sri Lankan stocks, buoyed by across-the-board buying by local and foreign investors, crossed the psychologically important 800-point barrier on Tuesday to close at a 26-month high, brokers said.
The Colombo all share index closed 8.2 points higher at 804.2, closing above the 800-mark for the first time since April 12, 1995.
"The psychological mark was broken without any resistance," said Sanjeeva Gunewardena of Ceylinco Stock Brokers. "There were very optimistic buyers in the market."

Turnover was a high 346.8 million rupees, boosted by a pre-arranged foreign crossing of three million Asian Hotels shares at 13.75 rupees, about 28,000 John Keells Holdings shares at 300 rupees and 165,000 development bank DFCC shares at 285.
National Development Bank rose by 10 rupees to 255 rupees on 136,400 shares and Hayleys gained 10 to 260 rupees. Foreign purchases amounted to 234.2 million rupees.

"Some stocks may reach the over-valued mark if this trend continues," said Nandakumar Nair, an analyst with John Keells Stock Brokers. "But it is not likely to go through a correction because of the positive sentiment in the market."
